criteria.short: Aunt Frances shops for a new pair of shoes for a party.
criteria.intro: Der Prüfling nennt sinngemäß, z. B.:
bullets: Aunt Frances goes shopping because she wants a new pair of shoes to wear to a neighbour's party.

criteria.short: The shoes she likes are all expensive.
criteria.intro: Der Prüfling nennt sinngemäß, z. B.:
bullets: She can't buy a lot of the shoes because they're all expensive.

criteria.short: The man shows her other shoes on special offer.
criteria.intro: Der Prüfling nennt sinngemäß, z. B.:
bullets: The man in the shop shows her other shoes that are on special offer.

criteria.short: The white shoes are too big.
criteria.intro: Der Prüfling nennt sinngemäß, z. B.:
bullets: The problem is that the white shoes are too big, so she can't walk right in them.

criteria.short: He tells her to wait and gets other shoes.
criteria.intro: Der Prüfling nennt sinngemäß, z. B.:
bullets: The man tells her to wait and goes to get some other nice shoes.

criteria.short: She thinks they are great/perfect and loves them.
criteria.intro: Der Prüfling nennt sinngemäß, z. B.:
bullets: Aunt Frances thinks the black shoes are great/perfect, and she loves them.

criteria.short: The shoes belong to another woman.
criteria.intro: Der Prüfling nennt sinngemäß, z. B.:
bullets: The problem is that the black shoes belong to another woman, so Aunt Frances can't buy them.

criteria.short: Where does she often go?
bullets: Where does she often go?

criteria.short: "What shoes do you like?"
bullets: "What shoes do you like?", asks the shop assistant.

criteria.short: Where does the shop assistant work?
bullets: Where does the shop assistant work?

criteria.short: "When do you wear comfortable shoes?"
bullets: "When do you wear comfortable shoes?", asks the shop assistant.

criteria.short: What does the other woman own?
bullets: What does the other woman own?

criteria.short: What does the shop sell?
bullets: What does the shop sell?

criteria.short: Form: am/is/are + Verb-ing correctly stated.
bullets: SUBJ. + am/is/are + VERB+ing + O + place + time

criteria.short: Signal word 1 named correctly.
bullets: now

criteria.short: Signal word 2 named correctly.
bullets: at the moment

criteria.short: Signal word 3 named correctly.
bullets: Look!/Listen!/right now

criteria.short: 8 correct present-progressive sentences describing the picture.
criteria.intro: Erwartete Inhalte je Bildelement, z. B.:
bullets: 1 A man is speaking on the phone.
2 A woman is looking for something.
3 A boy is trying on new shoes.
4 A woman is paying for her clothes.
5 An old man is reading a newspaper.
6 A girl is showing a backpack to a woman.
7 A girl is holding a teddy bear.
8 A boy is lacing up his new shoes.
schema: Je Satz 2 P: 1 P korrekte **present progressive**-Form (am/is/are + -ing), 1 P passender Inhalt/Wortschatz zum Bildelement

groups.titel: Simple present oder present progressive (16 Lücken)

criteria.short: 16 Lücken korrekt: simple present oder present progressive je nach Signalwort.
bullets: are happening, is walking, takes, is running, is sitting, reads, is talking, are playing, meet, is kicking, is eating, drops, is playing, stop, is watching, are enjoying
schema: Je Lücke 0,5 P: korrekte Zeitform passend zum **Signalwort** (usually/often/always/sometimes → simple present; now/today/at the moment/right now/Listen! → present progressive)

criteria.short: Vielfältiger Wortschatz, alle geforderten Ausdrücke verwendet.
schema: Verwendung der geforderten Ausdrücke: **go along**, **turn right**, **straight ahead/on**, **past**, **on the right(-hand side)**, **opposite**

criteria.short: Korrekte Grammatik: Imperativ, Präpositionen, Fragebildung.
schema: Korrekte Fragebildung mit **How do I get to...?**

criteria.short: Sprachrichtigkeit: Rechtschreibung, Satzbau.
Weg laut Karte korrekt und vollständig beschrieben.
bullets: Go along Station Street.
Turn right into King Street.
Go straight on, past the sports shop and the restaurant.
Tom's Café is on the right, opposite the church.
